notes: OKA (oka.com/uk). Same Graphene HC API method as Bestsellers (POST /api/js/query, theme 38caf17c88c5431c932b42cdc117b64e, template id 'category', X-Referer + X-Requested-With headers required to resolve the real collection - verified via header.category_id matching each collection's true Shopify id from /collections.json). Discovery: grepped /collections.json for new/arrival synonyms, then confirmed structure by reading the site's own header mega-menu on a fetched collection page. The nav exposes a genuine 'New' concept: dropdown heading 'Explore New In' -> 'Shop All New' (/collections/new, title 'New In') with real children 'New Furniture', 'New Homeware', 'New Lighting' in the dropdown itself, plus 'New Soft Furnishings' surfaced as a signposting link on the /collections/new hub page (same clc-Signposting block as New Furniture/Homeware/Lighting) - all four are genuine PLPs with their own product grids, so kept as children of New Arrivals. Two other links in the same 'New' dropdown were inspected and excluded: 'New Wallpaper' points to /collections/wallpaper, whose actual Shopify title is plain 'Wallpaper' (not a 'new' handle/title - it is the site's standard Wallpaper category page merely promoted under the New menu, no new-arrivals taxonomy signal); 'New OKA X Lewis & Wood' points to /pages/oka-x-lewis-wood, a marketing/collaboration page, not a collection. 'Back in Stock' (/collections/back-in-stock) was also seen in the same dropdown and excluded - it denotes restocked availability, not newly-added-to-catalogue, and is not one of the brief's target terms. Note: the four children's product_count values (46+88+35+28=197) sum to MORE than the parent New In listing (166) - this is the site's own reported data (not a computation on my part), so both parent and children are recorded as-is per the brief's overlap rule; it suggests 'New In' is a differently-curated feed rather than a strict union of the four children.
